evals.name: plan-phase-1
evals.prompt: We're in the bakery-ops repo and Phase 0 is done. Plan Phase 1 (ordering and the live kitchen/bar screens). Write the plan file the way this project expects and tell me what has to be true before anyone writes Orders code.
evals.expected_output: A docs/phases/phase-1-plan.md following the phase-plan template: contract tests listed first (orders->inventory reserve/release/consume + Availability::bulk, orders->catalog Prices::at snapshot + stationFor, orders->identity short code / acting-as / PIN, payments->orders totals), migrations with NUMERIC scales, action endpoints with permissions and idempotency, events, intra-phase build order, test list incl. Playwright p1-order-flow and p1-shortfall, Phase1Seeder, ADRs 0006/0007. The agent stops for approval instead of coding and says plan_approved must be set by Ramin.
expectations: Produces docs/phases/phase-1-plan.md (or equivalent plan document) with sections for contract tests, migrations, endpoints, events, build order, tests, seeds, ADRs
Lists consumer-side contract tests BEFORE Orders implementation and names Reservations::reserve/release/consume or equivalent Inventory capabilities as the thing to prove first
States that Payments in Phase 1 is a schema-complete skeleton where only cash can pass validation (no photo upload yet)
Mentions that the plan needs Ramin's approval (plan_approved) before coding begins and does not start implementing Orders
Migrations specify decimal(12,2) for money and decimal(14,4) for quantities, and include branch_id and client_uuid on orders
Quotes the output of gate_check.py --mode entry (or phase_status.py show) rather than only describing the state
Uses the manifest's capability names verbatim (Reservations::reserve/release/consume, Prices::at, Routing::stationFor) instead of invented service names
Lists all four Phase 1 contracts from the manifest (orders->inventory, orders->catalog, orders->identity, payments->orders) and marks payments->orders as intra-phase

evals.name: refuse-phase-2-start
evals.prompt: Can we start Phase 2 now? I want to begin the production module today.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the entry preflight (gate_check.py --mode entry --phase 2 or reads STATUS.json equivalently), sees Phase 1 is not done (gate-p1 red / no done_commit) and refuses to start, naming the red Phase 1 gate and the missing production contracts, and lists exactly what must happen first. It does not create Production code.
expectations: Answers no / not yet rather than starting Phase 2 work
Names the Phase 1 gate (gate-p1 or gate:p1) as not green or Phase 1 as not done as the blocking reason
Names the missing contract tests for Production (production->inventory, production->catalog, production->identity) or the unapproved Phase 2 plan as further prerequisites
Does not create any files under app/Modules/Production
Refers to gate_check.py --mode entry (or runs it) as the mechanism for this decision
Pastes the gate_check entry output verbatim with the FAIL lines (not a paraphrase)
Orients with phase_status.py show (or equivalent STATUS read) before answering and names the next in-order step of the current phase

evals.name: place-production-module
evals.prompt: Add the production module: bakers get production requests when a cake runs out, accept them, log the batch, and the cake becomes available again. Where does this go and how do we build it so it doesn't break anything?
evals.expected_output: The agent places Production in Phase 2 (step 2.7), lists its dependencies with named capabilities (Inventory Stock::of + Ledger::appendMany atomic + StockOut event; Catalog scaled recipe + default_batch_qty; Identity assignedUsers/isOverseer; Notifications by event only), explains the cycle break with Shifts via the StationPresenceResolver / ShiftAttacher interfaces instead of importing Shifts, and prescribes contract tests first, then module tests, then implementation, ending with gate_check --mode module.
expectations: Places the module in Phase 2 and names its build-order position after purchases/transfers/notifications or cites manifest step 2.7
Lists dependencies on Inventory, Catalog and Identity with at least one named capability each (e.g. Ledger::appendMany, Recipes::activeFor scaled by yield, assignedUsers)
Says Production must not import Shifts and names the interface-based cycle break (StationPresenceResolver / ShiftAttacher or AssignedUsersResolver / NullShiftAttacher)
Prescribes writing consumer-side contract tests before any Production code
Mentions Notifications are reached by domain events, not by importing Notifications models
Lists all four Phase 2 contracts required by the manifest (production->inventory, production->catalog, production->identity, notifications->identity)
Uses the manifest capability names (Ledger::appendMany, Recipes::activeFor scaled by yield, assignedUsers, isOverseer) rather than invented ones
Does not propose hand-editing STATUS.json (plan_approved, module status or phase) to make progress

evals.name: explain-or-fix-ci
evals.prompt: CI is red on my PR for the inventory module: mod-inventory failed, and so did mod-orders, e2e-p1 and gate-p1. Which one do I fix and why is the pipeline shaped like this?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the needs: chain mirrors the module dependency graph, so mod-inventory is the lowest failing job and the only one to fix; downstream failures are consequences. It notes mod-inventory also runs consumers' contract tests (contract:orders->inventory etc.), so the break may be a contract regression rather than an inventory unit test, and points at scripts/ci/pest-groups.sh / the module-tests reusable workflow and local parity via python scripts/task.py ci.
expectations: Identifies mod-inventory as the job to fix first and the others as downstream consequences of the needs chain
Explains that the job graph mirrors the module dependency graph (identity -> catalog -> inventory -> orders ...)
Mentions that the inventory job also runs consumer contract tests (contract:orders->inventory or similar) so a consumer expectation may be what broke
Suggests reproducing locally with the same steps (python scripts/task.py ci / make ci or the pest group)
States that with current_phase 0 the Phase 1 jobs are skipped by the status job, not failed, and that gate-p0 is the blocking required check
Cites the manifest ci.module_jobs / gate_jobs or references/ci-cd.md as the source of the job graph

evals.name: real-start-shared-module
evals.prompt: Start Phase 0 step 0.2: build the Shared module (branches, stations, BranchScoped, Bilingual cast, Quantity/Money value objects, StateMachine trait, Idempotency middleware with its table, ActorContext) with its tests, inside the repo rules.
evals.expected_output: Real code under apps/api/app/Shared with migrations using decimal(14,4)/(12,2), branch_id on stations and idempotency_keys, unit tests for Quantity/Money/StateMachine, arch and invariant tests still green, and scripts/check_invariants.py --all clean. The agent runs the checks via Docker (scripts/pest or task.py), not host PHP, and updates STATUS via phase_status.py module shared in_progress.
expectations: Creates migrations for branches, stations and idempotency_keys with branch_id on stations and idempotency_keys
Quantity and Money value objects use brick/math BigDecimal (no float arithmetic)
Adds unit tests for Quantity/Money arithmetic and StateMachine illegal transitions tagged with the unit group
Runs or instructs running tests through Docker (scripts/pest, scripts/artisan or task.py), never host php
python scripts/check_invariants.py --numeric --branch-id --bilingual reports zero violations on the result
gate_check.py --mode entry --phase 0 was run and reported PASS before any Shared code was written (evidence in RESPONSE.md)
Tests were committed before implementation (a red-tests commit precedes the implementation commits in the branch history)
gate_check.py --mode module --module shared reports PASS and phase_status.py module-stable shared was run (STATUS.json shows modules.shared.status = stable)
Idempotency middleware and ActorContext each have passing tests tagged module:shared

notes: Iteration 2 (2026-10-19): assertions extended to skill-only process behaviour after iteration 1 showed the repo infrastructure alone satisfies the outcome assertions. Baseline copies must keep .claude/skills/bakery-ops-builder/assets (manifest) so scripts run; fixtures should state their premise in README-EVAL.md.
